reasons: Both answers make the same core diagnosis (Redis visibility_timeout redelivery of ETA tasks), refuse to credit any single change, and propose a reproduction with a shortened visibility_timeout followed by enabling the changes one at a time. B also names the single worker as a gap in the local test, includes several workers in its reproduction, runs a control on the old code with a raised timeout, and says the test was never run against the old commit, which covers rubric item 2 more fully. A adds a quick task_id log check, which is useful, but neither answer explicitly recommends deploying with monitoring for duplicate sends and keeping the ticket open until that is confirmed.

B: Implies that a single worker cannot receive a redelivered task, but Redis can redeliver it to the same worker, so the single-worker point is overstated
